Hi Amit,

Thanks for the clear list 94 this is great context. High-level answers up front, then a suggested activation path: 

- 18-month term: Yes, AWS Marketplace private offers support non-standard term lengths. We typically model >12-month terms as a multi-year commitment in the private offer metadata; finance will need to sign off on proration for partial first/last months. There’s no Marketplace technical blocker, but we do record the term on the offer and billing will follow that cadence.

- Pilot then convert: Starting with a time-limited pilot (3 months) and converting to a longer private offer is common. For co-sell eligibility, the key is buyer activation and the Marketplace listing status: if the private offer is accepted by a buyer account during the pilot, they’re counted as an active customer for co-sell tracking. Converting later does not retroactively affect the co-sell flag.

- Buyer approval path: recommended sequence below. This minimizes delays for signature and AWS activation: 
  1) Procurement signs initial PO for pilot (procurement@healthgrid.com) 
  2) Program owner (product lead) approves technical scope (internal) 
  3) CFO signs for conversion to >12mo (if required by your finance policy) 
  4) Buyer account accepts private offer in AWS Console (we provide activation link)

I’ve attached a short checklist with the Marketplace acceptance steps and internal roles (healthgrid_po_summary.xlsx). I’m looping in Neha (partner ops) to confirm co-sell readiness and Vivek (co-sell lead) to weigh in on the eligibility signal we need to surface to AWS.

Next steps: if you can share the proposed procurement language and whether HealthGrid requires proration rules for an 18-month term, we’ll run it by Finance and Legal and give you a firm playbook.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Amit 94 great, glad that maps to your org. Short answers and an action pack below: 

- Pilot conversion clause: Yes, we can include an "option to convert" clause in the pilot PO that preserves the agreed pricing for conversion to an 18-month private offer. Our legal team prefers a simple clause that references the original pilot PO number and the conversion window (we typically allow conversion within 30 days of pilot end).

- PO fields for smooth activation: please include these minimal fields on the pilot PO so AWS and Redwood can match the acceptance: 
  * Redwood offer ID (we will provide)
  * Pilot PO number (your internal number)
  * Billing contact + email
  * Estimated start date and pilot length (3 months)

Action pack (what I’ll send today):
- Draft DocuSign envelope with pilot PO + conversion clause (I’ll share to procurement@healthgrid.com)
- AWS private offer activation link (one-click buyer accept)
- Short checklist for co-sell readiness (attached: aws_private_offer_checklist.pdf)

Neha/Vivek, please confirm if any additional co-sell requirements are necessary on our side before we request AWS co-sell enablement. If we get the acceptance within the pilot window, co-sell tracking should be automatic but we want to ensure we surface the right customer metadata to AWS.

Amit/procurement: expect DocuSign tonight. I’ll follow up with the offer ID once AWS confirms the private offer is created.

Thanks,
